title: Sentrylet: decision-weaver for automated frontline remediations
creator: Avery Collins
description:
Goal: Build 'Sentrylet' — a lightweight decision-weaver service that converts runbook fragments (shortflow tasks) into safe, observable automated remediations for first-line support.

Context: We have many ad-hoc admin utilities and runbook snippets used by SRE/Support. Operators want a low-friction path from 'manual shortflow' to an automatable, permissioned micro-remediation that can be executed automatically or offered as a one-click suggestion in the ops console. Sentrylet should:
- Accept typed runlet inputs (safe param schema) and an execution policy.
- Evaluate preconditions, rate/quota checks, and guardrail rules (RBAC + artifact provenance).
- Optionally run in dry-run mode and surface diffs to the console and telemetry.
- Emit structured telemetry and a canonical execution record for auditing and replay.

Scope & non-goals:
- Scope: runbook-to-task adapter, decision evaluator, policy gate, audit record, console hook (UI shim only).
- Non-goal: not the full orchestration layer for long-running multi-step remediations (that remains runflow).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Sentrylet can ingest a runlet fragment (YAML JSON schema) and validate params.
2) It enforces precondition checks and returns a deterministic decision object (allow/deny/suggest) with reasons.
3) When allowed, Sentrylet produces a signed execution bundle that the shortflow runner can consume.
4) Dry-run mode produces a diff and a safety score; telemetry shows decision latency and false-positive rate baseline.
5) End-to-end test with sample shortflow: 'truncate-staging-cache' executed via canary user group with audit events in logstore.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Decision engine will be rules-first (policy DSL) with a small plugin hook for ML-based risk-scoring later. Rules allow fast auditability and deterministic behavior.
- We will reuse existing RBAC and audit log plumbing from admin-proxy service to avoid duplicating sensitive paths.
- To keep latency low, runlet validation + decision evaluation will be bounded to 150ms 95p in the common case; throttles applied for heavier checks.
- Signed bundles use current HSM/KMS integration; key rotation compatibility must be ensured.

Data & telemetry:
- Emit decision.event with: runlet_id, user_id, decision, reasons[], latency_ms, safety_score, dry_run boolean, execution_bundle_id.
- Add an internal dashboard slice in Console under 'Ops > Sentrylet' (P0 metric: decision latency; P1 metrics: decisions/deny rate, blocked by RBAC).

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal engineering-runbook-only, dry-run enforcement for 1 week.
2) Beta: enable canary group (on-call) with 'suggest' UI in Console and manual approve -> execute path.
3) Full: allow auto-execute for low-risk runlets with rate caps and rollback hooks.

Testing & validation:
- Unit: policy DSL parsing, param schema validation.
- Integration: shortflow runner consumes signed bundles; audit log appears in logstore.
- Chaos: simulate key rotation and response-time spikes.
- Safety: create a set of 12 'high-risk' templates that must always require two-step approval.

Deliverables:
- Service: sentrylet API + policy DSL runtime.
- Console: minimal 'suggestion card' UI hook and dry-run diff viewer (UI owner to supply wireframes).
- Telemetry: Grafana dashboard + alert for decision latency > 300ms 95p.

Rollforward/backout: if audit or safety issues found, feature flags allow immediate revert of auto-execute and throttle to manual-suggest only. Full disable path via runtime config in admin-proxy.
